title: Moving in big steps
goal: Get anywhere on a line or in a file in a few keystrokes, and insert exactly where you mean to.

lessons.title: Word and line motions

concepts.desc: one character or line at a time. Vim also maps these to h j k l; arrows work just as well. The goal this week is to need them less.
next word start / previous word start / end of word. Punctuation counts as its own word.
the same for WORDS: anything between spaces (foo.bar(baz) is one WORD).
back to the end of the previous word.
line start / first non-blank character / line end.
delete the character under the cursor.

lessons.tip: If you press ← or → more than twice in a row, stop: there's a word motion that gets you there faster.

quiz.q: Cursor at the start of `foo.bar(baz) next`. Which single key jumps straight to `next`?
What's the difference between `0` and `^`?
quiz.a: 0 goes to column 0; ^ goes to the first non-blank character (they differ on indented lines).

quiz.q: Which key moves to the end of the current/next word?
How many `w` presses from the start of `a.b c` to reach `c`?
quiz.a: 3 (a, ., b and c are separate words: w lands on ., then b, then c).

quiz.q: Which key goes back to the start of the previous WORD?
Cursor anywhere on a line: how do you get to the last character?

lessons.title: Insert where you mean

concepts.desc: insert before / append after the cursor.
insert at the first non-blank / append at the end of the line, from anywhere on it.
open a new line below / above and enter insert mode.
resume inserting where you last left insert mode. Use it when you stop typing to fix or check something elsewhere: gi takes you back, in insert mode, from wherever you are.
delete the word / everything typed on the line, without leaving insert mode.

lessons.tip: Never do `$a` or `0i`: A and I do it in one key. Never do `j0i<CR>`: that's what O and o are for.

quiz.q: From the middle of a line, which key appends at the end of the line?
How do you add a new line above the current one and start typing?
What does `I` do on an indented line?
quiz.a: Inserts before the first non-blank character (after the indentation).

quiz.q: What does `gi` do?
quiz.a: Goes back to where you last left insert mode and enters insert mode there.

quiz.q: In insert mode, you typed a wrong word. Which key deletes it without leaving insert mode?
Difference between `i` and `a`?
quiz.a: i inserts before the cursor character, a after it.

lessons.title: Big jumps through a file

concepts.desc: first line / last line.
go to line N (e.g. :42 or 42G).
previous / next blank line (paragraph boundary).
scroll half a page down / up.
top / middle / bottom of the visible screen.
scroll so the cursor line is centered / at top / at bottom.
jump to the matching ( ) [ ] { }.

lessons.tip: Holding ↓ to scroll is a slow mouse wheel. Use } to hop by block, Ctrl-d to page, :N when you can see the line number.

quiz.q: How do you jump to line 120?
What does `}` do?
quiz.a: Moves to the next blank line (end of the paragraph/block).

quiz.q: Cursor on a `{` - which key jumps to its matching `}`?
How do you scroll half a page down?
The cursor line is at the bottom of the screen and you want it in the middle. Which keys?
Which key moves the cursor to the top line visible on screen?

lessons.title: Small fixes, undo and redo

concepts.desc: replace the character under the cursor with c (stays in normal mode).
toggle case of the character and move right. A count works: 3~.
toggle / upper / lower case of the whole line.
join the next line onto this one, fixing up the whitespace.
delete the character under / before the cursor.
undo / redo. Each insert session is one undo step.
most commands take a count: 3x, 5j, 2w, 8~.

lessons.tip: Leave insert mode often. Every insert session is one undo step, so short inserts make undo precise.

quiz.q: How do you change a single `a` into `o` without entering insert mode?
What does `J` do?
quiz.a: Joins the next line to the current one, replacing the line break and leading whitespace with one space.

quiz.q: Redo after an undo?
Uppercase the whole current line?
Delete the next 4 characters?
What exactly does one `u` undo after you typed a sentence in insert mode?
quiz.a: The whole insert session (everything typed between entering and leaving insert mode).
